extracted.intended_audience: United States Congress, executive policymakers, and informed public interested in national defense reorganization
extracted.subtask_description: Presidential recommendations and standards for reorganizing the U.S. armed forces into a unified Department of National Defense, with principles for structure, civilian control, budgeting, training, research, and personnel. Aimed at guiding legislation and executive implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrated strategic plans and a unified military program and budget
rubrics_metrics.description: We should have integrated strategic plans and a unified military program and budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategy, program, and budget are aspects of the same basic decisions. Using scientific and intelligence advice, estimate probable nature of future attack, determine organization and deployment, and allocate manpower, material and financial resources consistent with an over-all plan. Separate departmental programs and budgets (Army and Navy) should be planned as a whole rather than piecemeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economies through unified control of supply and service functions (eliminate duplication)
rubrics_metrics.description: We should realize the economies that can be achieved through unified control of supply and service functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duplication between Army and Navy activities has produced waste: separate buyers, different specifications, separate inspectors, parallel transport and storage. Pooling requirements reduces margins of safety for supplies, facilities, personnel and construction; unified systems of supply reduce required reserves as volume increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt organizational structure suited to coordinate military policy with other national programs and foreign policy
rubrics_metrics.description: We should adopt the organizational structure best suited to foster coordination of military policy with foreign policy, industrial mobilization, scientific research, and intelligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Military policy must be consistent with foreign policy (including United Nations commitments), adjusted to diplomatic success, and reflect knowledge of other powers' intentions. A comprehensive security program requires participation by many agencies; fewer departments simplify top-level coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide strongest means for civilian control of the military
rubrics_metrics.description: We should provide the strongest means for civilian control of the military by concentrating responsibility in a single full-time civilian below the President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One Cabinet member (Secretary of National Defense) with clear primary responsibility strengthens civilian control; divided secretaries have restricted views and may act as partisans. Traditional democratic practice—civilian subject to the will of the people—prevents militarism if exercised properly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize to provide parity for air power
rubrics_metrics.description: We should organize to provide parity for air power, recognizing that its responsibilities equal those of land and sea power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parity for air power can be achieved in one department or in three, but not in two; a single department is preferred to three. Air power must receive equal organizational status in strategic planning and execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a unified system of training for combined operations
rubrics_metrics.description: We should establish the framework for a unified system of training for combined operations of land, sea and air.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combined operations require officers and men to understand capabilities, procedures and limitations of other services. Training determines conduct in combat; integrated training programs, merged training activities, and cross-assignment of officers produce necessary joint experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematically allocate limited resources for scientific research
rubrics_metrics.description: We should allocate systematically our limited resources for scientific research to avoid duplication and focus talent on the most promising lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given limited scientific talent, apply it to weapons and research with greatest potential regardless of service. Preserve initiative and enterprise while eliminating duplication and misdirected effort; this requires top-level co-ordination among services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of command at outlying bases
rubrics_metrics.description: All military authority at each outlying base should be placed under a single commander with clear responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single commanders at outposts ensure clear accountability for security and unified employment of reconnaissance, radar, intelligence and counter-intelligence rather than separate service authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent and equitable personnel policies across services
rubrics_metrics.description: We should have consistent and equitable personnel policies to eliminate competition and inconsistency between services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differences existed in recruitment, promotion rates, officer selection, utilization of reserves, awards, allowances, and discharge point systems. A unified organization will minimize such disparities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single Department of National Defense with full responsibility for armed national security
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be a single Department of National Defense charged with the full responsibility for armed national security, incorporating forces and civilian elements of the War and Navy departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislation should prescribe broad top-level authorities and permit development of detailed departmental elements over time by the President and Secretary; unification is a long-term job requiring evolving organizations, doctrine and habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civilian Secretary of National Defense and subordinate civilian leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: The head of the new department should be a civilian Cabinet member designated as the Secretary of National Defense, supported by a civilian Under-Secretary and assistant secretaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civilian leadership below the President fixes civilian control. Under-Secretary and assistants should be assignable to duties determined by President and Secretary; civilian staff should be strong to exercise real control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational structure must permit fixing responsibility at top levels
rubrics_metrics.description: The department should have an organizational structure which will permit fixing responsibility at the top levels of unified department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide Secretary with ample authority to establish central coordinating and service organizations (military and civilian). Some elements may be assistant-secretary-managed, central service organizations, or top military staff — the precise nature to be developed by executive leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three coordinated component branches under assistant secretaries
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be three coordinated branches of the Department of National Defense: land forces, naval forces, and air forces, each under an assistant secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Navy should retain carrier and water-based aviation; the branches are coordinated components within the unified department rather than fully separate departments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a Chief of Staff for the Department and commanders for each component
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be a Chief of Staff of the Department of National Defense and a commander for each of the three component branches—Army, Navy and Air.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Chief of Staff and the three commanders should constitute an advisory body to the Secretary and to the President; civilians may communicate with component commanders on vital matters. Key staff posts should be filled with officers drawn from all services to avoid domination by any one service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rotation and limited tenure for Chief of Staff
rubrics_metrics.description: The post of Chief of Staff should be rotated among the services when practicable and the tenure should be relatively short—two or three years—and not extended except in a declared war emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short, rotating tenure helps prevent dominance by any single service and aids evolution of unified thinking during the department's formative period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide authority to establish central coordinating and service organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: The President and the Secretary should be provided with ample authority to establish central coordinating and service organizations where necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such organizations might be under assistant secretaries, organized as central service organizations, or as top military staff; sufficient strength in department-wide elements versus separate service elements will ensure meaningful unification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create or promote a Federal Research Agency for defense-related fundamental research
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a Federal Research Agency among whose responsibilities should be promotion and co-ordination of fundamental research pertaining to the defense and security of the nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A government-wide research agency would help coordinate fundamental military research and apply scientific findings across services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a co-ordinated government-wide intelligence system
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a co-ordinated, government-wide intelligence system to support consistent political and military policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An integrated intelligence system should be advanced; additional action will be taken as the advisability of broader coordinated security programs becomes clear.
